dependency_assessment.observed_transfer: An origin-produced public receipt records one named fleet runtime sending a unique controlled-canary request to a second named fleet runtime. The recipient-side watcher records consuming that exact receipt.
dependency_assessment.recipient_use: The recipient sends a distinct acknowledgement whose correlation fields point back to the original canary request, and the origin runtime's public receipt lists the same acknowledgement. This is a concrete temporal and semantic dependency, not merely similar text or shared infrastructure.
dependency_assessment.event_time: The origin receipt says the canary began at 2026-07-23T22:46:46Z, records the observation window from 22:46:47Z through 22:46:48Z, and timestamps the correlated acknowledgement at 22:46:48.866Z.
dependency_assessment.publication_time: Pull request 525 opened at 2026-07-23T22:49:09Z and stated the controlled-canary success criteria. Commit ea5362f04616b5b919426e79422f2f2c47c5385b published the receipt and implementation at 2026-07-24T03:24:06Z; the pull request merged one second later.
dependency_assessment.participant_limit: The agent names, runtime binding and model or provider labels are origin-authored. They distinguish roles inside the record but are not provider-owned authentication of independently operated principals.
dependency_assessment.operator_limit: The pull request says a human account dispatched the work to a headless coding agent, verified the work and required a separate project gate before merge. The repository protocol prescribes the reviewers and task-gate authorities, while official project material places a human founder above the fleet with a final seal.
dependency_assessment.task_limit: The exchange is an expressly controlled regression canary and returns a protocol acknowledgement. It does not show an unrequested task result, artifact transfer or recipient effect outside the assigned acceptance condition.
dependency_assessment.current_activity_limit: The October repository head and current product pages show continuing project development, but the July receipt alone does not authenticate that the two historical runtimes remain active or coordinated now.

provenance_limits: The canary JSON is an origin-produced receipt committed several hours after the claimed event; no independent service or provider attestation was located.
The public record demonstrates delivery, consumption and a correlated acknowledgement, but it does not expose a task-result artifact whose semantic content causes a later independent effect.
The receipt records one matching acknowledgement, while the merge message retains at-least-once and concurrent-consumer caveats. It is not used here as proof of global exactly-once behavior.
A fleet role, model label, reviewer identity or agent UUID does not by itself prove a separate operator. Raw UUIDs are omitted from this publication.
